13.assets: Exact gland/body/locknut/seal/compression nut, matched cable, ordinary enclosure panel and actual tightening tools. Select one LAPP family/SKU and cable range before fixing dimensions; no commercial CAD or force value is claimed yet.
13.physics: Fixed panel as ordinary installed enclosure; cable flexible enough for real axial/torsional response; actual threads or a disclosed causal thread model; elastomer seal compression must couple tightening to real retention. No magic attachment when score crosses a threshold.
13.phases: Acquire/route cable through the correct loose components → fit body/locknut to panel → position actual seal → thread compression nut while restraining body/cable as required → tighten to the verified OEM procedure → release → evaluator performs a benign calibrated retention check.
13.score: Proposed tiers: 0.25 for correct undamaged component/cable assembly, 0.5 when gland is secured to panel and seal/nut correctly seated, 0.75 after retention proof, 1.0 after all declared completion conditions remain released and stable. Wrong/missing seal cannot earn full credit. No IP/waterproof rating is inherited; if sealing is claimed, add the real prescribed seal test.
13.measurement: Photographs with scale for component seating and cable mark; visible nut datum or measured OEM tightening requirement; spring-scale pull with displacement mark. Fix actual load/tolerance after manual/hardware calibration, not by inventing an OEM number.
13.reset: Release compression, inspect actual seal for permanent damage, restore same cable marks and loose component order; replace seal/cable if the real procedure consumes/damages them. Restore panel mounting.
13.negatives: Nut looks seated with seal absent; cable supported by fingers; cable outside permitted range; body rotates during tightening; nut bottoms before clamping; valid alternate assembly order; safe temporary repositioning; false retention from cable welded to fixture.
13.cpu: Start with stock-gripper access and thread/torque/reaction measurements. Exercise seal compression versus measured cable-slip behavior, then actual robot joint actions over the full path. A rigid cable welded to the gland, as in the routing comparator, cannot establish this task.
13.stop: Stop if no genuine fitting/retention procedure can be reproduced, if stock tool access/torque fails or if another earlier gland-assembly task matches.

85.assets: Exact ECHO Speed-Feed family head, actual eyelets, internal spool/catch and correct nylon line; retain actual full-size supported trimmer/tool interface where OEM loading expects it. No prewound cassette substitution.
85.physics: Passive spool/knob rotation, actual line-routing passages and feed/locking mechanism, deformable line with contact/friction and realistic bending. Model only geometry supported by the exact manual/hardware; never script line segments into a final wound pose.
85.phases: Align OEM loading indicator → pass line through actual eyelets → equalize exposed ends → hold real housing and turn winding knob through legitimate grasps/regrasps → leave allowed leader lengths → release → perform the prescribed benign feed/readiness check.
85.score: Proposed tiers: 0.25 for genuine passage through both proper eyelets, 0.5 for correctly engaged winding, 0.75 for correct exposed leaders, 1.0 for working feed/retention after release. Winding progress must be physically observable/functional, not just a counted knob angle.
85.measurement: Ruler for exposed leaders, visible alignment/engagement marks, and an OEM-consistent feed/release test. Hidden internal wraps must be inferred only by a legitimate functional check or provided ordinary inspection access, not simulator coordinates.
85.reset: Unwind/remove through the actual permitted release; inspect line abrasion and replace consumed line; restore empty head/indicator and unthreaded line. Do not silently retain successful wraps across resets.
85.negatives: Line merely draped through eyelets; unequal ends masquerade as full spool; knob turns without pulling line; prewound hidden spool; failed feed despite good external lengths; finger support; benign tail contacts/table overhang must not automatically erase valid progress.
85.cpu: First actual knob torque and stock grasp; then short contact-verified threading/first-turn prototype; only then full actual line length and complete robot-controller diagnostic. Long thin line may dominate collision cost and make this slower than other leads.
85.stop: Stop if the actual head only permits an inaccessible control, if an earlier same-kind line-loading benchmark is found or if a causal flexible-line model cannot preserve feed behavior.

5.assets: One exact commercially documented window frame/glazing system, real pane, gasket and actual matching bead profile; ordinary glazing supports and OEM-permitted hand/block/mallet tool. Choose actual available sizes, not a scaled-down frame.
5.physics: Preserve bead toe, groove undercut, retaining lip and gasket contact. Disclosed compliant/contact approximation may replace difficult polymer flex only if it preserves the real insertion/retention skill. No pose-triggered weld.
5.phases: Orient bead → engage required toe/end → progressively rotate/press/tap using actual allowed tool → seat all required length/corners → release → inspect profile and retention without holding pane/bead.
5.score: Proposed 0.25 for valid toe engagement, 0.5 for actual partial retained length, 1.0 for complete correct bead/gasket retention and released state. Do not count a flush-looking but unhooked strip or a gripper-supported bead.
5.measurement: Side/end photos and depth/straightedge measurement of proudness, plus a justified gentle retention check at accessible locations. Numerical thresholds come from selected profile/physical build. No unsupported claim that every window bead uses the same method.
5.reset: Remove using the actual bead-release procedure and permitted tool; restore intact gasket/pane support and initial bead pose. Replace any damaged profile; no forced reverse collision reset treated as a physical method.
5.negatives: Bead reversed, toe in wrong slot, middle pressed but ends loose, real gasket pinched, hand holds final strip, rigid box stand-in has no actual undercut, impossible access because glazing blocks the tool.
5.cpu: Test exact profile contact and required insertion force before robot motion. Then test stock-gripper/tool access for one short real section and progress to complete actual-size assembly; do not claim the short coupon validates full reach.
5.stop: Stop if normal installation requires unachievable load/reach or earlier glazing revisions already contain the same bead-refit objective.

62.assets: Actual-size training arm, real-style bladder/fabric cuff with marker/index range and authentic closure; no rigid cuff arches or prewrapped starting state. Patient circulation and diagnosis outside scope.
62.physics: Preserve wrap path, textile bending/stretch and hook-and-loop retention. A disclosed contact/adhesion model is acceptable only if loose, folded or wrongly tensioned fabric can genuinely fail. Rigid arch placement cannot substitute.
62.phases: Acquire cuff/locate marker → wrap actual arm with controlled slack → tension and close genuine overlap → smooth without trapping folds → release → inspect OEM fit and retained location.
62.score: Proposed 0.25 for meaningful partial wrap, 0.5 for closed retained cuff, 1.0 only with correct marker/index/edge positions, flat bladder region and proper fit after release. Avoid demanding a particular hand sequence or rewarding visual size choice alone.
62.measurement: Ruler and photos at defined marker/index/edge locations plus the OEM fit check; benign inflation only if specified and needed to inspect fit, never a fabricated medical diagnostic result. Exact dimensions/fit tolerances await the actual cuff instructions.
62.reset: Open cuff normally, inspect closure, restore unwrapped flat starting cuff and same arm posture. Do not preload tension or retain hidden fold state.
62.negatives: Rigid arch over beam; prewrapped cuff; unsupported self-adhesive pose constraint; marker displaced; sleeve folded underneath; closure retained only by robot; correctly fitted alternative wrapping technique; wrong size-selection logic without physical fitting.
62.cpu: Actual closure/shear and fabric bending tests first; then two-arm wrap path with measured joint/gripper actions. Deformable-material work is likely expensive and is why this is not one of the first two builds.
62.stop: Stop if an earlier genuine cuff-wrapping task matches; if only pose-based arches can be simulated; or if stock fingers cannot grasp the real cuff edge/closure.

77.assets: One actual robot-joint encoder installation: matched magnetic ring/readhead, OEM bracket/fasteners and approved gauge/spacer. A generic dial on a block cannot borrow robot-building importance.
77.physics: Rigid joint/ring/bracket geometry, actual adjustment degrees of freedom and screw clamping; gauge carries real clearance/contact. Any simulated signal model must derive from physically relevant pose/gap, with limitations explicit.
77.phases: Locate ring/joint datum → place actual setup gauge → align readhead/bracket while engaging real fasteners → secure without losing gap → remove gauge → release → perform benign joint-turn/signal/gap check per manual.
77.score: Proposed 0.25 for legitimate bracket placement, 0.5 for secured in-range gap, 1.0 for complete retained orientation/runout allowance and required functional check. No reward for simply moving a dial to a mark or reading a screen.
77.measurement: Actual approved shim/feeler/gap measurements and readable witness locations; if an OEM signal diagnostic is required, retain it as an ordinary test, not a fictional visual indicator. Precision values remain unset until source verification.
77.reset: Release bracket normally, restore loose fasteners and start offset/gauge, inspect contact surfaces, retain exact encoder calibration state and real joint datum. No scored target written into the mechanism.
77.negatives: Correct pointer but wrong physical gap; bracket moves when gauge removed; sensor touches ring during rotation; readhead aligned at one position but runout makes contact elsewhere; hand-supported final state; invented bracket/oversized knobs.
77.cpu: Gauge/contact geometry and stock screwdriver access first; fastener reaction and full rotation clearance next; then complete actual robot action sequence. No thermal, torque-rating or signal-accuracy claim from geometry alone.
77.stop: Stop if no exact robot-building application/manual exists, required precision/tool access exceeds YAM or a near-identical sensor-gap setup already exists.
